column2: Expected source population behind Tiler's recognized dtype catalog: the format-defining
specifications first, then the ecosystem spelling, exposure, and namespace-governance
precedents the same research cites. One row per preserved unit.
path: path under this directory, or "-" when no bytes are retained here.
sha256: digest over the exact retrieved byte stream, or "-" when no bytes were ever retrieved.
One retrieval source is not byte-reproducible; README.md names it and says why.
Provenance for each id — owner, edition, retrieval URL and date, licence, verdict — is in README.md.
`verify-sources.sh` enforces the row count, the per-classification counts, id uniqueness, every
vendored digest, and that no file on disk escapes this manifest.
Ecosystem spelling/exposure precedents and namespace-governance precedents. These documents
do not define a value set; they record how an existing system spells, exposes, or governs one.
Python array API standard 2025.12, cited by the operation and signature taxonomy rather than by the
dtype research. Preserved per chapter because the standard is a multi-document website, not one file.
MLIR Linalg definition files, the two operation interfaces they build on, and the enum file that fixes
what `iterator_types` may hold — cited by the operation and signature taxonomy for structured-operation
form. Same LLVM revision as the rows above, so they join `llvm-project-license-llvmorg-22.1.8` rather
than adding a second licence row.
